D1 — Does this empathy narrative match the real first-call journey?
Project/branch/task: main branch, /plan-devex-review of PLAN.md (SDK quickstart docs).
ELI10: Before scoring anything, I need to be sure I understand what a first-time developer actually goes through. I wrote a first-person walkthrough of the 8 declared steps, labeling what's declared vs. what I'm predicting (Postgres install, bun context switch, unknown key turnaround, unknown success output). If my picture is wrong, every finding downstream is aimed at the wrong pain.
Stakes if we pick wrong: I'd score and propose fixes for friction that doesn't exist while missing the friction that does.
Recommendation: A because the narrative only asserts the 8 declared steps and labels everything else as predicted or unknown.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
Pros / cons:
A) Accurate, proceed with this understanding (recommended)
  ✅ Review proceeds on the declared facts with predictions kept clearly labeled as predictions
  ✅ No time spent re-litigating a journey that the plan already spells out step by step
  ❌ Any unstated nuance (e.g., a fast key turnaround) stays unknown and gets scored as unknown
B) Some of this is wrong, let me correct it
  ✅ Corrections tighten the friction trace before it drives scores and remedies
  ✅ Lets you supply outputs, timings, or steps the plan omits so fewer items stay unknown
  ❌ Costs a round trip now; corrections only affect empathy context, not scope
C) This is way off, the actual experience is...
  ✅ Replaces the whole journey with your ground truth before any scoring
  ✅ Prevents a fundamentally misaimed review
  ❌ Requires you to describe the full journey from scratch
Net: Confirming or correcting the journey now is cheap; scoring the wrong journey is not.

reply: Confirmed persona: a hands-on developer making a first SDK call. The declared onboarding facts are: Step 1: clone the repo. Step 2: install bun manually if not present. Step 3: copy .env.example to .env and fill in 8 environment variables. Step 4: run database migrations against your local Postgres. Step 5: start the dev server. Step 6: open the docs in a separate tab. Step 7: register an API key by emailing the team. Step 8: paste the key into your .env, restart the server, then make your first SDK call. No quickstart command, no hosted sandbox, no copy-pasteable curl example. No measured turnaround, outputs, or runtime behavior were supplied. Keep predictions and unknowns labeled. This supplies persona and empathy context only; proposed fixes and scope changes remain undecided.
